topStories.headline: Landmark Affordable Housing Complex Opens at Former Haight Street McDonald's
topStories.dek: The long-awaited 730 Stanyan development celebrated its grand opening last month, delivering 160 units of affordable housing to the gateway of Golden Gate Park.
topStories.body:
After nearly a decade of planning, the affordable housing complex at 730 Stanyan Street held its grand opening on July 28–29, 2026, transforming a site long notorious for drug activity and crime into a home for 160 low- and moderate-income families. The location at Haight and Stanyan streets next to Golden Gate Park was once the site of a McDonald's restaurant that the city purchased in 2018 to completely transform.

The $153 million project was developed as a joint venture by Chinatown Community Development Center and the Tenderloin Neighborhood Development Corporation, in partnership with the city's Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development. The eight-story building offers units ranging from studios to three-bedroom apartments, all affordable, with some studios priced at around $600 a month and some three-bedrooms for around $2,300.

Of the 160 units, 32 are designated for residents who have experienced homelessness and 20 for transitional-age youth. Mayor Daniel Lurie and former Mayor London Breed both attended the opening ceremony. The project was designed by OMA architects and its facade features glass fiber reinforced concrete panels.

For residents like Mona Hamilton, who once slept at the site during its McDonald's era, the opening represented a profound personal milestone. All units at the complex are already filled, reflecting the acute demand for affordable housing in the Haight-Ashbury neighborhood and across San Francisco.

topStories.headline: Muni Boosts N-Judah and 5R Fulton Service Starting August 29
topStories.dek: SFMTA announces its most significant service improvements in years for routes serving the Haight and Cole Valley, taking effect in two weeks.
topStories.body:
Riders in the Haight, Cole Valley, and Panhandle neighborhoods will soon see tangible improvements to their daily commutes. The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency announced this week that a series of systemwide Muni improvements will take effect on Saturday, August 29, 2026, with key upgrades to routes that serve this cluster directly.

The N-Judah, Muni's busiest rail line and the primary service through Cole Valley, will see peak-hour frequency improve from every 10 minutes to every 9 minutes — a roughly 10 percent increase in capacity, according to SFMTA Director of Transportation Julie Kirschbaum. The 5R Fulton Rapid, which runs along the Panhandle corridor, will switch to larger 60-foot buses running every 10 minutes, restoring capacity lost earlier this year when 40-foot trolley buses were used following the closure of the Potrero bus facility.

The changes come despite the SFMTA's ongoing financial crisis, which the agency describes as the largest in its history. The board approved a two-year operating budget in April that closes a $307 million shortfall for fiscal year 2026-27 without cutting service. The SFMTA says it has identified approximately $250 million in cost savings through operational efficiency improvements, making the August 29 upgrades cost-neutral.

The service changes are also timed to support San Francisco Unified School District students returning to school on August 17. SFMTA representatives said the adjustments were based on rider feedback, operator input, and service performance data.

topStories.headline: Two Giant Crow Sculptures and a 'Cosmic Seed' Join the Panhandle as Part of Big Art Loop
topStories.dek: A citywide public sculpture initiative has installed two permanent-for-now artworks in the Panhandle, adding to a growing free 34-mile art trail through San Francisco's neighborhoods.
topStories.body:
The Panhandle — the narrow strip of green that connects the neighborhood to Golden Gate Park — gained two large-scale sculptures this spring as part of the Big Art Loop, San Francisco's ambitious citywide public art initiative. The works, installed in May 2026, are now on view free to the public and have quickly become neighborhood talking points.

'An Attempted Murder' by Northern California sculptor Jack Champion features two large-scale black bronze crows named Tom and Lucinda. Previously exhibited at the Smithsonian's Renwick Gallery, the piece is installed near Ashbury between Oak and Fell streets, where the artist says real crows — which have proliferated in the neighborhood — might even find themselves flattered by the oversize depictions. Nearby, at the western entry to the Panhandle, Brooklyn-based sculptor Kate Raudenbush installed 'Seed of Self,' a meditation sculpture shaped like a split seed with a laser-cut brass mandala and mirrored sphere; at night, internal lighting transforms it into a glowing beacon along the path.

The Big Art Loop is a free, 34-mile walkable and bikeable trail of large-scale sculptures threading through San Francisco neighborhoods, organized by the nonprofit Building 180 in partnership with the SF Recreation and Park Department and the SF Arts Commission. The Panhandle installations bring the total number of sculptures on the loop to 23, with more planned throughout the year.

Both sculptures are slated to remain in the Panhandle for at least one year, with the possibility of extension. The Haight Street Art Center and the North of the Panhandle Neighborhood Association both expressed public support for the project ahead of installation.

events.title: 'Forever Grateful' Grateful Dead Exhibition at Haight Street Art Center
events.location: Haight Street Art Center, 215 Haight St, Lower Haight
events.description: A landmark free exhibition celebrating the legacy of the Grateful Dead, featuring artwork, instruments, and memorabilia chronicling the band's history from 1965 to 1995. The show runs Thursday–Sunday at the Lower Haight nonprofit gallery before transferring to Golden Gate Park's Hall of Flowers on September 5.

events.title: Big Art Loop Sculptures: 'An Attempted Murder' & 'Seed of Self'
events.location: The Panhandle, near Ashbury & Oak/Fell, Haight-Ashbury
events.description: Two large-scale sculptures installed in May 2026 as part of San Francisco's free 34-mile Big Art Loop trail are on free public view in the Panhandle. Jack Champion's towering bronze crow pair and Kate Raudenbush's illuminated 'Seed of Self' metal sculpture are both accessible at all times.

events.title: Counterculture Museum — Ongoing Exhibitions
events.location: Counterculture Museum, 1485 Haight St (at Ashbury), Haight-Ashbury
events.description: The museum at the corner of Haight and Ashbury, named one of TIME's World's Greatest Places 2026, offers immersive exhibits on the 1960s counterculture, civil rights, women's liberation, and LGBTQ+ movements. Open Wednesday–Sunday; admission $10, reduced rates for students and seniors.

events.title: Cole Valley Night Market
events.location: Cole St & Carl St, Cole Valley
events.description: The free, family-friendly neighborhood night market returns to Cole Valley's commercial strip, featuring local food vendors, live music, local makers, and special activities. The market is presented by the Cole Valley Merchants Association in collaboration with Sunset Mercantile and Avenue Greenlight.

events.title: Muni N-Judah & 5R Fulton Service Improvements Take Effect
events.description: SFMTA's updated Muni schedules go into effect, with the N-Judah running every 9 minutes during peak hours and the 5R Fulton Rapid switching to larger 60-foot buses every 10 minutes — improvements directly benefiting riders in Cole Valley and along the Panhandle corridor.

events.title: 47th Annual Haight Ashbury Street Fair
events.description: San Francisco's beloved annual street fair returns free to Haight Street, featuring over 200 outdoor vendors, three stages of live music, food, local artists, green businesses, and a family zone. The fair stretches six blocks through the heart of the neighborhood.

events.title: 'Forever Grateful / Golden Gate Park' Opens at Hall of Flowers
events.location: San Francisco County Fair Building (Hall of Flowers), 1199 9th Ave, Golden Gate Park
events.description: The second installment of the Haight Street Art Center's landmark Grateful Dead exhibition opens at Golden Gate Park, featuring the Furthur Bus, Jerry Garcia's BMW, large-scale projections, live performers, puppetry, and community storytelling installations. Runs through October 25.

moreNews.headline: Haight Street Art Center's 'Forever Grateful' Grateful Dead Show Draws Crowds Through Summer
moreNews.body: The Haight Street Art Center at 215 Haight Street has been hosting 'Forever Grateful,' a landmark free exhibition paying tribute to the Grateful Dead's three-decade legacy, since July 3, 2026. The show features artwork, instruments, and memorabilia and runs Thursday–Sunday, noon to 6 p.m., through September 4 before a second, participatory installation opens at the Hall of Flowers in Golden Gate Park on September 5. The Golden Gate Park installment, developed in partnership with experiential performance company Third Rail Projects, will feature Ken Kesey and the Merry Pranksters' Furthur bus and Jerry Garcia's BMW.

moreNews.headline: SFMTA Cites $322M Budget Deficit as Backdrop to August Service Gains
moreNews.body: Even as SFMTA announces service improvements for riders on the N-Judah and 5R Fulton starting August 29, the agency continues to grapple with what it describes as the largest financial crisis in its history. The SFMTA board approved a two-year operating budget in April 2026 that closes immediate shortfalls of $307 million in FY 2026-27 and $344 million in FY 2027-28, largely through operational efficiency savings. However, the structural deficit is projected to grow to $430 million by 2030 without new revenue. Mayor Daniel Lurie has placed a Muni parcel tax on the November 2026 ballot that is expected to raise between $160 million and $183 million per year from property owners citywide.

moreNews.headline: Amoeba Music SF Hosts Live In-Store Event This Weekend
moreNews.body: Amoeba Music at 1855 Haight Street continues its tradition of free in-store performances, with Oakland singer-songwriter, producer, and vocalist Veotis scheduled to perform a live set and sign his latest album 'Feelings to Run From' on Sunday, August 16 at 2 p.m. Veotis is a former Amoeba SF employee whose artistry bridges hip-hop, R&B, soul, and jazz. Attendees can purchase the album at the store and get it signed after the set. Admission is free.

moreNews.headline: Counterculture Museum Marks First Year as TIME's 'World's Greatest Place'
moreNews.body: The Counterculture Museum at 1485 Haight Street — right at the corner of Haight and Ashbury — wrapped up a weeklong anniversary celebration in June 2026 marking its first year of operation, according to the museum's website. Opened in May 2025 by Jerry and Estelle Cimino, who also run the Beat Museum in North Beach, the 4,000-square-foot space was named one of TIME magazine's World's Greatest Places in 2026. The museum covers the psychedelic movement, Summer of Love, anti-Vietnam War activism, women's liberation, LGBTQ+ rights, and the Black Panthers, and features a small stage for readings and events. It is open Wednesday through Sunday, 11 a.m. to 6 p.m.; admission is $10.

restaurants.name: Zazie
restaurants.description: Beloved Cole Valley institution since 1992 serving Southern French country cuisine for brunch and dinner, with a heated garden patio and a proudly tip-free wage model.

restaurants.name: Magnolia Brewing
restaurants.description: Haight Street's beloved craft brewpub, back under local independent ownership since late 2024, serving house-brewed beers, cocktails, and elevated pub fare at Haight and Masonic.

restaurants.name: Cha Cha Cha
restaurants.description: A Haight Street classic since 1984, serving bold Caribbean-Latin tapas including jerk chicken, ropa vieja, and legendary sangria in a lively, eclectic setting with a heated backyard garden.

restaurants.name: The Alembic
restaurants.description: A cozy Haight institution known for expertly crafted cocktails, a thoughtful whiskey selection, and a seasonal menu of American small plates.

restaurants.name: Parada 22
restaurants.description: A neighborhood favorite bringing the vibrant flavors of Puerto Rico to Haight Street, with dishes like mofongo, pernil, and tostones.

restaurants.name: O'Reilly's Pub SF – Haight
restaurants.description: A lively Irish pub that opened in the former Milk Bar space, offering live music, comedy, and trivia seven nights a week alongside a full bar and bar bites.

restaurants.name: Escape from New York Pizza
restaurants.description: A Haight Street institution serving big New York-style pizza slices by the piece or whole pie, popular with locals and park-goers for decades.

restaurants.name: Zam Zam
restaurants.description: A legendary Haight Street dive bar famous for some of the city's best martinis, with a distinctive Persian-style interior and decades of neighborhood history.

restaurants.name: Trax Bar
restaurants.description: The Haight's only gay bar, a casual and friendly dive known for the signature Bitchin' Bloody Mary and a welcoming, spirited atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Abu Salim Middle Eastern Grill
restaurants.description: A neighborhood go-to for excellent hummus, shawarma wraps, and freshly grilled Middle Eastern fare in the heart of the Haight.

restaurants.name: Best of Thai Noodle
restaurants.description: A popular Haight Street Thai spot serving over 50 dishes of Thai cuisine for lunch and dinner, known for staying open late after a night out.

restaurants.name: Om Indian Cuisine
restaurants.description: A Haight Street Indian restaurant offering a well-regarded mix of vegetarian dishes and Northern Indian classics in a cozy setting.

restaurants.name: Kezar Bar & Restaurant
restaurants.description: Cole Valley's beloved sports bar steps from Kezar Stadium, known for surprisingly good food alongside an extensive beer selection and a convivial neighborhood atmosphere.

restaurants.name: The Gold Cane
restaurants.description: A Haight Street bar institution with a long history, offering classic cocktails and a laid-back atmosphere at the heart of the Upper Haight.

restaurants.name: Pork Store Café
restaurants.description: A popular Haight Street diner open since 1916 serving hearty American breakfast classics — omelettes, breakfast burritos, and pancakes — in a no-frills, welcoming setting.

restaurants.name: Haight Street Market
restaurants.description: A community-oriented neighborhood café and market in the heart of the Haight serving coffee, sandwiches, and provisions.

restaurants.name: Crepes on Cole
restaurants.description: A Cole Valley neighborhood staple serving sweet and savory French-style crêpes in a small, cheerful café steps from the N-Judah stop.

hotels.name: Stanyan Park Hotel
hotels.description: A Beaux Arts Victorian hotel listed on the National Register of Historic Places, built in 1904–05 across from Golden Gate Park, offering 36 individually decorated rooms with complimentary breakfast, afternoon tea, and weekday wine and cheese receptions.

hotels.name: The Metro Hotel
hotels.description: A family-owned, art-filled 23-room hotel on Divisadero Street in the heart of Haight-Ashbury, featuring original artwork, a serene garden, and a helpful local-knowledge staff just around the corner from Golden Gate Park.

hotels.name: 555 Haight Guesthouse
hotels.description: A small guesthouse in the Lower Haight neighborhood offering budget-friendly accommodation with easy access to local bars, restaurants, and transit.

shops.name: The Booksmith
shops.description: Haight-Ashbury's fiercely independent general-interest bookstore since 1976, known for exceptional curation in counter-culture, literary fiction, graphic novels, and politics, plus an acclaimed author events program.

shops.name: Amoeba Music
shops.description: A legendary, warehouse-sized Haight Street record store offering an unparalleled collection of new and used vinyl, CDs, and DVDs across every genre, plus regular free in-store performances.

shops.name: Cole Hardware
shops.description: An independent, locally owned hardware store that has served Cole Valley for decades, stocking tools, housewares, gardening supplies, and a helpful neighborhood-oriented staff.

shops.name: Say Cheese
shops.description: A Cole Valley institution beloved as one of San Francisco's best cheese shops, offering an expertly curated selection of domestic and imported cheeses, charcuterie, and accompaniments.

shops.name: Wasteland
shops.description: An iconic Haight Street vintage and consignment shop carrying carefully curated secondhand clothing, accessories, and footwear from the past several decades.

shops.name: Love on Haight
shops.description: A vibrant Haight Street boutique specializing in colorful tie-dye clothing and accessories celebrating the neighborhood's countercultural spirit.

shops.name: Grateful Dead Archive Store
shops.description: An officially licensed Grateful Dead merchandise and memorabilia store on Haight Street, offering a wide range of apparel, vinyl, prints, and collectibles.

shops.name: Piedmont Boutique
shops.description: A Haight Street fixture since 1972 known for its eye-popping window displays and eclectic selection of performance costumes, club wear, and wigs for all occasions.

shops.name: The Ice Cream Bar
shops.description: A meticulously restored 1930s soda fountain in Cole Valley serving artisan ice cream, handcrafted sodas, and classic egg creams in an atmospheric vintage setting.

shops.name: Haight & Ashbury Records
shops.description: A small independent vinyl shop on Haight Street specializing in rock, psychedelic, and classic soul records with a focus on used finds.

shops.name: Haight Street Market
shops.description: A community-focused neighborhood market stocking local provisions, wine, and specialty grocery items for residents of the Upper Haight.

artEntertainment.name: Counterculture Museum
artEntertainment.description: Opened in May 2025 at the iconic corner of Haight and Ashbury, this 4,000-square-foot nonprofit museum covers the 1960s counterculture — from the Summer of Love and psychedelic movement to civil rights, feminist, and LGBTQ+ activism — and was named one of TIME's World's Greatest Places 2026.

artEntertainment.name: Haight Street Art Center
artEntertainment.type: Nonprofit poster art gallery and print studio
artEntertainment.description: A Lower Haight nonprofit art space dedicated to San Francisco's poster and printmaking tradition, offering free rotating gallery exhibitions, a working screenprint studio, and community workshops; currently hosting the landmark 'Forever Grateful' Grateful Dead exhibition through September 4.

artEntertainment.name: Amoeba Music (Music Venue)
artEntertainment.description: Beyond its role as a legendary record store, Amoeba's Haight Street floor regularly hosts free in-store performances and artist signings across all genres, often timed to new releases and neighborhood events.

artEntertainment.name: Kezar Stadium
artEntertainment.description: A beloved 10,000-seat stadium at the edge of Golden Gate Park, built in 1925 and rebuilt in 1990, hosting high school sports, soccer, track and field, and community events; currently undergoing improvements to accommodate Golden City Football Club.

artEntertainment.name: The Booksmith (Events Venue)
artEntertainment.type: Independent bookstore and literary events venue
artEntertainment.description: In addition to its role as a landmark bookshop, The Booksmith hosts a celebrated year-round author events program featuring readings, book swaps, and literary conversations with nationally known writers.

artEntertainment.name: Kezar Pavilion
artEntertainment.description: An indoor arena adjacent to Kezar Stadium in the southeast corner of Golden Gate Park, available for sports events, community programs, and permitted group activities.

artEntertainment.name: The Panhandle
artEntertainment.type: Public park and outdoor art trail
artEntertainment.description: The narrow, tree-lined park connecting the neighborhood to Golden Gate Park, now home to two Big Art Loop sculptures — 'An Attempted Murder' and 'Seed of Self' — alongside free public green space, walking paths, and a beloved community gathering spot.
artEntertainment.address: Fell St & Oak St, between Stanyan & Baker

artEntertainment.name: Buena Vista Park
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's oldest park, set on a hill at the eastern edge of the Haight, offering panoramic views of the Golden Gate Bridge, bay, and downtown through a dense canopy of eucalyptus and Monterey pine.

gymsRecreation.name: HAUM Studios – Haight
gymsRecreation.description: An award-winning, queer-owned yoga studio steps from Golden Gate Park offering Vinyasa, Hatha, Restorative, Yoga Nidra, breathwork, and soundbath classes for all levels, plus private sessions and workshops.

gymsRecreation.name: BodyRok Haight
gymsRecreation.description: A Haight Street boutique studio offering high-intensity, low-impact 40-minute Sculpt pilates classes designed to tone and strengthen using reformer-style equipment.

gymsRecreation.name: Live Fit Gym – Cole Valley
gymsRecreation.description: A well-regarded independent neighborhood gym in Cole Valley offering strength training, cardio equipment, and personal training in a community-oriented environment.

gymsRecreation.name: Kezar Stadium Track
gymsRecreation.description: The publicly accessible running track at the historic Kezar Stadium, open daily from 6:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. and popular with neighborhood runners, walkers, and fitness groups.

gymsRecreation.name: Panhandle Park
gymsRecreation.description: The Panhandle's tree-lined paths and open lawns serve as a de facto outdoor gym for the neighborhood, with joggers, cyclists, yoga practitioners, and dog walkers sharing the green space daily alongside the new Big Art Loop sculptures.
gymsRecreation.address: Fell St & Oak St (Stanyan to Baker)

gymsRecreation.name: Koret Health and Recreation Center
gymsRecreation.description: The University of San Francisco's comprehensive recreation center near the Panhandle, offering a pool, gym, courts, and fitness classes open to the community through membership.

gymsRecreation.name: Buena Vista Park
gymsRecreation.description: San Francisco's oldest park provides hillside hiking trails with panoramic city and bay views, popular for trail running and outdoor fitness among Haight-Ashbury residents.

gymsRecreation.name: Kundalini Yoga Center
gymsRecreation.description: A dedicated Kundalini yoga center near the Haight offering classes integrating breathwork, mantra, and movement for practitioners at all levels seeking a more spiritual yoga practice.
